stem: In eukaryotic cytoplasm, what are the net carbon products of glycolysis starting from one glucose before mitochondrial oxidation?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Jumps to complete aerobic oxidation of glucose.
options.explanation: Full oxidation to six CO2 requires pyruvate processing plus citric acid cycle turns.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acetyl-CoA forms after pyruvate enters mitochondria and is processed by the pyruvate dehydrogenase path.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None; glycolysis cleaves glucose into two three-carbon pyruvates.
options.explanation: OpenStax Biology notes glycolysis begins with glucose and produces two pyruvate molecules (plus ATP and NADH carriers).

options.label: D
options.misconception: Confuses glycolysis with pyruvate dehydrogenase oxidative decarboxylation.
options.explanation: CO2 release occurs during pyruvate oxidation and the citric acid cycle, not glycolysis itself.

options.label: E
options.explanation: Lactate appears only if NADH is reoxidized by fermentation rather than the electron transport chain.

context: Learning objective: recall glycolysis carbon products. Glycolysis is anaerobic and cytosolic; it yields two pyruvates.
imageCaption: Cellular respiration: glycolysis -> pyruvate -> acetyl-CoA -> citric cycle carriers -> ETC/ATP synthase; O2 terminal acceptor; fermentation regenerates NAD+.
